problems.quote: In a US study of 2,293 people aged 70 and over on medical wards, 35 in 100 left hospital less able to wash, dress, eat, get in and out of bed or use the toilet than two weeks before admission.
problems.fix: Split: "A US study followed 2,293 people aged 70 and over on medical wards. 35 in 100 left hospital less able than they were two weeks before admission. The five tasks were washing, dressing, eating, getting in and out of bed and using the toilet."

problems.quote: The data are over 20 years old, but a 2020 review of studies in adults aged 65 and over found about 3 in 10 lost independence in basic daily activities after an acute hospital stay, with little change by the year the study began.
problems.fix: "The data are over 20 years old. A 2020 review of studies in adults aged 65 and over found about 3 in 10 lost independence in basic daily activities after an acute hospital stay. That share changed little by the year the study began."

flags: Sentence 3 "23 in 100 had lost that ability" - 'that ability' is vague (which of five tasks?) and the 23+12=35 link is left for the reader to add.
'Improving since admission can be true' is a mild setup claim, but answered at once; acceptable.

problems.quote: 23 in 100 at 70 to 74, 63 in 100 at 90 and over (crude figures)
problems.fix: The figure 23 in 100 already means something else earlier (declined before arrival, not regained). Fix: "By age, the share who went home less able than before the illness was 23 in 100 at 70 to 74 and 63 in 100 at 90 and over (not adjusted for other differences)."

problems.quote: In a US cohort of 2,293 people aged 70 and over admitted to medical wards (Covinsky 2003), 35 in 100 went home less able in basic daily activities (washing, dressing, eating, getting in and out of bed, using the toilet) than they had been two weeks before admission.
problems.fix: Split into two sentences after "medical wards (Covinsky 2003)."

problems.quote: A 2020 review (Loyd, J Am Med Dir Assoc) pooling studies of 7,375 adults aged 65 and over found that about 3 in 10 lost independence in basic daily activities after an acute hospital stay, with little change by the year the study began, though results varied widely between studies.
problems.fix: Split at "stay." and give the variation and the year trend as separate short sentences.

problems.quote: Another 20 in 100 declined before admission and got the ability back.
problems.fix: Reconcile: "That makes 35 in 100 in all (23 plus 12). A further 20 in 100 had declined before admission but had recovered by discharge, so they are not in the 35." Also say the review's 3 in 10 comes from different studies and is close to the 35 in 100.

flags: Very long for one post; the 35/23/12/20/63/3-in-10/7,375 figures compete.
"Crude figures" and "Judgement:" are labels the reader must decode.
Closing line is a limit, acceptable, but the action sentence is buried before it.

problems.quote: Most had lost it before arrival.
problems.fix: "23 of those 35 had lost it before arrival and had not regained it." (both figures are in the x version)

problems.quote: In a US study of 2,293 medical inpatients aged 70+ (data over 20 years old), 35 in 100 went home less able to wash, dress or use the toilet than two weeks before admission.
problems.fix: "A US study followed 2,293 medical inpatients aged 70 and over (data over 20 years old). 35 in 100 went home less able to wash, dress or use the toilet than two weeks before admission."

flags: 'Most' has no number; 'it' refers to the ability only by inference.

problems.quote: In a US study of 2,293 medical inpatients aged 70+, 35 in 100 went home less able to wash, dress or use the toilet than two weeks before admission. 23 in 100 lost it before arriving and had not regained it by discharge.
problems.fix: Shorten: "A US study followed 2,293 medical inpatients aged 70 and over. 35 in 100 went home less able to wash, dress or use the toilet than two weeks before admission." then the 23 in 100 sentence.

flags: "can hide loss" is a figurative verb and 'loss' is not yet defined at that point.

problems.quote: In a Baltimore study of women in their 70s who were among the more able of their age group (1990s), those who had changed how or how often they walked or climbed stairs, without difficulty, were already slower and weaker.
problems.fix: "A Baltimore study in the 1990s followed women in their 70s who were more able than most of their age. Some reported no difficulty but had changed how or how often they walked or climbed stairs. These women were already slower and weaker than women who had not changed."

flags: Opens with a quoted question and answer used as a setup, answered by the post.
No size of the later risk is given ('more likely'); acceptable for X but the comparison group (women with no change) is only implied.

problems.quote: Among women who reported no difficulty at the start, those who had changed how they walked or climbed stairs had about 3 to 4 times the odds of developing difficulty over the next 18 months, even after allowing for walking speed (Fried 2000).
problems.fix: Split: "Some women reported no difficulty at the start. Those who had changed how they walked or climbed stairs had about 3 to 4 times the odds of developing difficulty over the next 18 months. This held after allowing for walking speed (Fried 2000)."

problems.quote: A later analysis found new changes predicted new walking difficulty a year and a half on, with wide uncertainty (Weiss 2012).
problems.fix: Either delete this sentence and keep the Fried 2000 figure only, or say in plain words how it relates: "A later analysis pointed the same way but with wide uncertainty."

problems.quote: A smaller Finnish study of people aged 75 to 81 found a similar pattern in men and women over 2 years (Mänty 2007).
problems.fix: Acceptable length; keep after the cut above.

flags: Opens with quoted question as a setup, answered by the post.
Three study results (Fried 2001, Fried 2000, Weiss 2012) on one effect without reconciliation.
"Judgement: it belongs in a functional history" - 'it' refers to a question two paragraphs earlier.

problems.quote: changing method without difficulty went with slower walking and later difficulty
problems.fix: "women who had changed how they walked or climbed stairs, but reported no difficulty, walked more slowly and were more likely to develop difficulty over the next 18 months."

problems.quote: A smaller Finnish study agreed.
problems.fix: "A smaller Finnish study of people aged 75 to 81 found a similar pattern."

problems.quote: later difficulty

flags: Opens with a quoted question as a setup.

flags: Opening question used as a setup, answered by the post.

problems.fix: "16 studies followed 42,775 older people living at home. They were reassessed after about 4 years on average (range 1 to 10). 14 in 100 became less frail. 29 in 100 became more frail. 57 in 100 stayed the same."

problems.fix: "Among people who were frail, 40 in 100 improved to the early stage, called prefrail. Only 3 in 100 lost all signs of frailty."

flags: "Being told you are frail describes where you are now. It can change." - reassuring opening; the post itself shows worsening was about twice as common as improvement, but never says so plainly.

problems.quote: A US study of 754 people found the same: going straight from frail to not frail at all was very rare, under 1 in 100 in each 18 months.

problems.quote: Reaching none of the frailty signs was far more common from the early stage (called prefrail) than from frailty. Among people who were prefrail, about 23 in 100 later showed none of the frailty signs, while about 18 in 100 became frail.
problems.fix: "People who were prefrail were much more likely to lose all frailty signs than people who were frail. About 23 in 100 prefrail people later showed none of the signs. About 18 in 100 became frail."

flags: Numbered list used for three numbers; fine, but the post is long for a phone.

flags: 'first' and 'Guidelines' unqualified (which guidelines, first what).

problems.quote: 3 in 100 to none
problems.fix: "3 in 100 lost all signs of frailty"

problems.quote: A Clinical Frailty Scale score of 6 can mean moderate dementia with prompting to dress, or intact thinking with a physical disability that means someone must stand by.
